key_insight: Dilute nitrogen incorporation in epitaxial LaFeO3 couples defect formation and lattice expansion to nearly 100-fold higher initial oxygen evolution activity.
engineering_relevance: This water-oxidation study, rather than AI or solar-cell research, suggests anion–defect engineering can enhance earth-abundant perovskite electrocatalysts.
method: Grow epitaxial LaFeO3−xNy films using nitrogen-plasma-assisted pulsed laser deposition.
Use ab initio calculations to assess coupled nitrogen substitution and oxygen/iron vacancies.
Evaluate electrical transport, OER kinetics, and post-reaction compositional changes.
evidence_signal: At <0.8% N/O, films show pronounced lattice expansion, predominantly bulk Fe3+, and nearly two orders of magnitude higher initial OER activity than undoped LaFeO3.
watch_item: The highly active as-grown state is metastable: near-surface nitrogen depletion and metallic iron oxidation/removal accompany rapid initial activity decay.
paper_title: Nitrogen Defect Coupling in Epitaxial LaFeO3 From Structural Reconstruction to Water Oxidation
